newsitem.title: HUNGARY: TVK says sales prices boosted H1 results.
newsitem.headline: TVK says sales prices boosted H1 results.

text.p: Hungarian chemicals Tiszai Vegyi Kombinat Rt (TVK) said it boosted its profits in the first half of the year by raising the prices of its polymer products by rates above the market average.

TVK said earlier on Thursday its net income rose to 8.02 billion forints in the first half of 1997 from 5.35 billion in the same period of 1996, while it increased its net sales to 40.68 billion forints from 31.08 billion.
The company said in a statement that world market trends were favourable and it had been able to exploit their impact by effective purchases, sales and management.
TVK said the average world market price of its raw material, chemical benzine, was 12.5 percent higher in the first half of the year than in the comparative period of 1996.

The average world market price of TVK's polymer products rose at a lower rate, with LDPE (low-density polyethylene) gaining 11 percent, HDPE (high-density polyethylene) nine percent and PP (polypropylene) four percent.

However, TVK increased its average foreign currency exports prices on foreign markets in the first half of the year by 20 percent for LDPE, 17 percent for HDPE and 16 percent for PP, the company said.
"This is mainly the result of the effective operations of new foreign trade subsidiaries," it said.
The strengthening of the dollar against the forint boosted these figures to 43 percent for LDPE and to 38 percent for HDPE and PP, the company added.
On the domestic market, TVK boosted its sales prices by 26 percent for LDPE and HDPE and by 33 percent for PP.
Inflation ran at 18.7 percent in June.
Domestic sales accounted for 45 percent of all sales, down from 50 percent in the first half of 1996.
TVK produced 51,600 tonnes of LDPE, 90,700 tonnes of HDPE and 74,000 tonnes of granulated PP in the first half of the year, figures almost unchanged from the first half of 1996.
